label: D1 after a rare a2->S1 transition that was rewarded
explanation: Fires only at D1, never at GO or D2, and almost only when the reward input is 1 (96% of mass). The strongest activations come at the D1 right after the agent chose a2, made a rare transition to S1 and got rewarded: the predicate covers 91% of top-quartile activations, with dev precision 0.83, recall 0.41 and mass recall 0.70. Adding the agent own upcoming choice (action == 2, i.e. it keeps a2 rather than switching to a1 as a model-based agent would) raises precision to 0.97 but lowers recall (F1 0.52), so I recorded the predicate that uses only observed variables. The remaining activations are weaker: moderate (about 0.3-0.5 of max) at D1 after runs of rewarded common a1->S1 trials, and tiny (<0.15) at D1 after unrewarded trials that follow a2->S1 rare trials. Broader predicates like rewarded at S1 (F1 0.32, mass 0.84) or any rewarded D1 (F1 0.18) are much less precise. The value head did not help separate firing from non-firing. Roughly: a rewarded-at-S1 signal that is largest when S1 was reached through the rare a2 transition.
